_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoking: Editing a file on your site

description: Apply literal find/replace edits to one file in one call, for small changes where uploading the whole file is wasteful. Each edit states how many matches it expects; any mismatch aborts the call with no writes. Served-file (dist) edits go live at once; source edits ship with build_and_deploy. Use apply_edits for several files.

edits.description: Ordered edits `{find, replace, count?}`, applied together; if any match count differs, nothing is written.

count.description: Expected matches: default 1 (fails on 0 or more than 1), -1 = replace all, or an exact number.

find.description: Literal text to find (not a regex). Max 64 KB.

replace.description: Literal replacement; empty string deletes the match. Max 64 KB.

name.description: Site name as shown by list_sites, e.g. my-portfolio.

path.description: Path inside the chosen tree, e.g. index.html.

target.description: 'dist' (default) edits the served file, live at once. 'source' edits the editable source tree; build_and_deploy ships it.

name: update_file_content

find.description: Echo of the input find. Truncated to 80 chars in the response for readability.

replacements.description: Actual number of occurrences replaced for this edit.

warnings.description: Secret-scanner findings in the rewritten file that did not block the edit (AWS Access Key, Stripe Key, JWT Token, etc.). Malicious content blocks the edit with MALICIOUS_CONTENT instead.

title: Surgical find/replace in one file
